source_title: Boeing posts third annual loss in a row as Dreamliner costs hit $5.5 billion (CNBC)
publisher_issuer: CNBC; corroborated by Boeing 10-K disclosures (787 deferred production costs) and Reuters/AP coverage of the 787 delivery halt
company_context: Boeing's 787 Dreamliner program experienced repeated production and quality defects that forced a near-total halt in deliveries for much of 2021 into 2022 while Boeing reworked aircraft and won FAA sign-off. The program also carries large 'deferred production costs' (capitalized cost above expected revenue on early units) that sit in inventory and must be recovered from future deliveries, a textbook operational/throughput bottleneck with a financial overhang.
business_type: Capital-intensive commercial aerospace manufacturing; complex global supply chain with program (deferred-cost) accounting
geography: United States (global supply chain and customers)
time_period: 787 delivery halt and abnormal-cost recognition 2021-2022; deferred-production-cost balance reported through subsequent 10-Ks
macro_context: Post-737 MAX crisis regulatory scrutiny, pandemic-era widebody demand weakness, and heightened FAA oversight slowing delivery sign-off.
outcome_category: 8 - operational disruption / margin and cash drag
evidence_summary: Quality defects (including fuselage join and structural tolerances) forced Boeing to halt most 787 deliveries for much of 2021, building undelivered inventory and triggering recognition of about $5.5 billion in 787 abnormal costs disclosed with Boeing's Q4 2021 results, contributing to a third consecutive annual loss. The program also carries large 787 deferred production costs in inventory; as of December 31, 2024, about $11.2 billion of 787 deferred production costs, unamortized tooling, and other non-recurring costs were expected to be recovered from units with firm orders, plus about $3.3 billion from expected future orders. This is an operational throughput/quality bottleneck that converted into a multi-billion-dollar cost and cash drag.

source_backed_metrics.consecutive_annual_losses: third annual loss in a row (through FY2021)
source_backed_metrics.delivery_disruption: near-total halt of 787 deliveries for much of 2021 due to production/quality defects

owner_decision_context: Management had to choose between continuing deliveries and pausing to rework aircraft and satisfy FAA quality requirements, accepting near-term throughput loss and abnormal-cost recognition to protect long-run program integrity.
action_taken: Halted most 787 deliveries through 2021 to inspect and rework aircraft, recognized about $5.5 billion in 787 abnormal costs, cut production rates, and worked to clear inventory and resume deliveries under FAA oversight.
outcome_evidence: Recognition of about $5.5 billion in 787 abnormal costs, a third consecutive annual loss through FY2021, undelivered-aircraft inventory build, and roughly $11-15 billion of 787 deferred production costs awaiting recovery from future deliveries confirm an operational bottleneck with a sustained financial drag.
source_limitations: WebFetch of CNBC and sec.gov returns HTTP 403 here; figures verified from search snippets of CNBC and Boeing 10-K disclosures rather than full-text read. The $5.5 billion is the reported 787 abnormal-cost figure tied to Q4 2021; the deferred-production-cost balances are as of December 31, 2024 and are program-accounting figures, not cash losses.
directly_stated: Boeing disclosed approximately $5.5 billion in 787 Dreamliner abnormal costs with Q4 2021 results
It was Boeing's third consecutive annual loss (through FY2021)
787 deliveries were largely halted through 2021 due to production/quality defects
About $11.224 billion of 787 deferred production costs (firm orders) and about $3.324 billion (expected future orders) were in inventory as of December 31, 2024
inferred: The root issue is an operational throughput/quality bottleneck rather than a demand failure (firm-order backlog remained large)
Deferred-cost recovery depends on future delivery throughput, tying the financial overhang to operational execution

Tests whether OpsIQ identifies operational_bottleneck and quality-driven throughput loss, separates it from demand_generation_failure (backlog stayed strong), and treats deferred-cost recovery as dependent on execution. Useful for modeling production constraints and capex/program risk.
